question: The insoluble substance formed in a solution during a chemical reaction is known as___________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Precipitate__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **insoluble substance** is created by a **chemical reaction or by the crystallization of a dissolved substance** to **form a precipitate**, both of which are solids that are formed from a solution.
 
• A solid substance that was once dissolved in a solvent like water becomes less soluble in the first scenario.
 
• **This may occur when:**
 
 
• The solution's temperature is reduced.
 
• The addition of a precipitating agent.
 
• The substance is mixed with still another, less soluble solvent.
 
 
 
• The **solution becomes supersaturated, and a precipitation reaction takes place** when the substance's solubility falls below its concentration.
 
• Any chemical reaction that results in an insoluble or **extremely poorly soluble product in the solvent** is considered a second instance.
 
• The solution soon reaches saturation once this product starts to develop, and the solid starts to precipitate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The particle size and characteristics of the solid are influenced by the rate at which precipitates occur.
 
• **Three different types of precipitates** can be recognized based on the size of the particles and the type of substance that is precipitating:
 
 
• Crystalline precipitates
 
• Cheesy precipitates
 
• Gelatinous precipitate
